overview.title: A Quieter Square in the Blue Alleys
overview.p1: Place El Haouta is one of the smaller squares in the medina, a short walk from the bustle of Place Outa el Hammam. Its main feature is a fountain covered in zellige tilework, surrounded by a handful of cafés and traditional houses painted in the usual blues and whites.
overview.p2: It is a good spot to slow down. Take a table, order a mint tea and watch the day pass. The fountain and the surrounding walls make for good photos in soft morning or afternoon light, when the square is quiet.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Place El Haouta

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: It is inside the medina, a few minutes on foot from Place Outa el Hammam. Ask a local or follow the signs.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Mornings and mid-afternoons are the calmest. Evenings are lively, so go earlier for peace and photos.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: Check prices before ordering and carry small cash. Be polite when photographing people.

q1.question: Where is Place El Haouta?
q1.answer: Inside the medina of Chefchaouen, a short walk from Place Outa el Hammam.

q2.question: Is Place El Haouta worth a stop?
q2.answer: Yes, if you want a quieter break with a pretty fountain. It is small, so a short stop is enough.

q3.question: Can I have tea at Place El Haouta?
q3.answer: Yes, a handful of cafés surround the square and serve mint tea and light snacks.

q4.question: What is the best time to visit Place El Haouta?
q4.answer: Morning or mid-afternoon, when it is quiet and the light is soft.
